clusters.title: Wording about the beam's own weight is misread: 'does not include beam weight' becomes NEGLECT, 'beam weight not included' and 'its own weight' / 'plus the weight of a W16x26' are not read at all + A positive phrase is matched inside its own negation or neglect instruction: 'not a W16', 'not an interior/edge beam', 'not braced against sidesway', 'neglect shear lag'
clusters.root_cause:
[self-weight-wording] reader.js neglectSelf() (2093-2101) treats a STATEMENT that the load leaves the weight out as an instruction to neglect it. (1) Alternative 1 'not\s+include' (2094) has no subject check, so 'does not include beam weight' / 'the dead load does not include the weight of the beam' match. (2) The last alternative '\bdead\s+load\b[^.;]{0,24}?\bincluding ...weight' (2100) skips the 'not' in 'dead load of 1 klf not including beam weight' and in '(not including the beam weight)'. selfMentions() correctly gives kind 'not' (= add), but all three users veto on neglectSelf: beamAnalysisFields 2195 (named beam), FILL.beam_select 2279 (self_weight_recheck) and FILL.beam_max_live_load 2320-2322 (include_self_weight=false, high). (3) The bare passive '(beam weight not included)' / 'self wieght not included' (no is/are) is read by neither SELF_PASSIVE_RE (2055 needs is/are) nor neglectSelf (needs a second 'weight'), so the page treats the text as if it never mentioned the weight and asks nothing. (4) addSelf() (2087-2092) does not know 'carries only its own weight' or 'plus the weight of a W16x26'. I confirmed all 10 still fail on cloud 448cad5 and probed the functions on the branch.
[negated-qualifiers] Each reader rule matches a positive phrase with no look at the words in front of it. FILL.beam_select 2284: a single W family named sets allowed_depths = [that depth], even after 'not a', 'except', 'other than', 'do not use' (the excluded W16X40 / W18X40 is printed). floorBits 2387/2388: the edge/inter regexes match inside 'is not an interior beam' / 'not an edge beam', so the tributary width is wrong by 2x. maySway 343-349: line 344 deletes 'braced against sidesway' out of 'not braced against sidesway', so the final \bnot\s+braced\s+against\b test can never match; the braced K 0.65 is used (599 printed for 293). tensionCommon (~1690-1736) has no rule for 'neglect / ignore / no shear lag', so Table D3.1's U = 0.90 is used (596.2 for 662.4).
clusters.fix_plan:
[self-weight-wording] reader.js only, in neglectSelf/addSelf plus one ask. (1) In neglectSelf, after the alt-1 exec, drop the match when 'not include' is a statement: the slice before it ends in does / doesn't / 'doesnot', or in a load subject (load(s)|it|this|that|which|they|these|values) + 'do'. The imperative 'do not include' / 'don't include' at a clause start stays NEGLECT. (2) The last alternative's span may not cross not/without: (?:(?!\bnot\b|\bwithout\b)[^.;]){0,24}?. I prototyped (1)+(2) on a scratch copy and ran all 4,718 corpus questions: 9 change, every one to the right value (178/179/22/33/102/169: 409.73; 31: W21X48; 70: W18X40; 32: 219.4; noise-144: W14X26) and nothing regresses. (3) addSelf, kind add: '\bcarr(?:y|ies)\s+(?:only\s+)?its\s+own\s+weight' and '\b(?:plus|and|in\s+addition\s+to)\s+(?:the\s+|its\s+)?(?:own\s+weight|self[- ]?weight|weight\s+of\s+(?:the\s+|an?\s+)?(?:beam|W\s?\d+\s*[xX]\s*\d+))'. The named-beam rule (2195) then takes the weight from the single shape: ANSWER 121.8 (96) and 111.56 (151). With no single named shape, beam_select uses the existing recheck; otherwise ASK. BC-095 'In addition to its own weight' also reads this way. (4) The bare passive '(?:self|beam|member)[- ]?w(?:ei|ie)ghts?\s+not\s+included' with no is/are has two readings: A2-beam-232 puts the same words after the blank, where they mean 'answer without it'. ASK with kind 'need'. In beam_analysis, ask for self_weight_plf ('type the beam's own weight in lb/ft, or zero if it is to be ignored', no digits in the text). In beam_max_live_load, ask for include_self_weight with the existing yes/no choices, now kind 'need'. This gives ASK for 180 and 231 and never the silent default. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'neglect / ignore / disregard self weight'; the imperative 'do not include the beam weight' (neglect); 'including its own weight' right after a load (has); 'beam weight is not included' (SELF_PASSIVE kind 'not' = add, already 232.53); her Q20 '(Include the self-weight of the beam in your calculation.)' (add); C-28's 'including the framing' rule (floor fills 2410-2416); a decimal load '0.5 klf not including beam weight' (already right, A2-beam-13).
[negated-qualifiers] reader.js, four local hunks. (1) beam_select 2284: test the 25 characters before the family for (?:\bnot|\bexcept|other\s+than|\bbut\s+not|\bexcluding|do\s+not\s+use|don't\s+use|\bavoid)\s+(?:an?\s+|the\s+)?$ (a slice test; ES5 has no lookbehind). When it is negated, allowed_depths = the nominal W depths list (as in the nominal-depth rule just below) minus that depth, with the rule text 'every W family but W16': ANSWER W18X40 (134) and W21X44 (152). (2) floorBits: a position phrase with not / isn't / no in the 20 characters before it is not a position word. The existing position ask then runs (it blocks on floor_plan: 'Beam position is required') and offers interior / edge / custom. ASK, because 'not interior' may be edge or a custom width (10, 11). (3) maySway: first .replace(/\b(?:not|never)\s+braced\s+against\s+(?:side[\s-]?)?sway\b/gi, ' unbraced against ') before line 344's deletion. 143 then gives ANSWER 293 (the page's own 'sidesway not prevented' route), and variant 171 (fixed-pinned, K 2.1) refuses on KL/r > 200; I checked that on the branch. (4) tensionCommon: '\b(?:neglect|ignore|disregard)\w*\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:effects?\s+of\s+)?shear\s+lag\b|\b(?:assume\s+)?no\s+shear\s+lag\b|\bshear\s+lag\s+(?:may|can|is\s+to|should)\s+be\s+(?:neglected|ignored)\b' sets U = 1.0 as given (like uStated): ANSWER 662.4 (149), and Ae 13.59 for the Ae variant. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'must be a W16', 'W16 only', 'lightest W16'; 'is an interior beam', 'edge beam', a beam with no position word (asks); 'braced against sidesway', 'sidesway prevented', 'unbraced frame'; 'use Table D3.1', 'find U', '(u=1)', and the cover-U exclusion at 1722 (a question that names shear lag).

clusters.title: A beam's end fixity or a partial-span load is not read, and the engine's default simple span is used silently (fixed-free, built into a wall, fixed at one end, fixed-pinned, both ends fixed, load over the left half)
clusters.root_cause: [beam-support-and-load-layout] reader.js beamAnalysisFields (2172-2179) sets support only from /\bcantilever(?:ed)?\b/ or 'simply supported|simple span|simple beam'. Anything else leaves the support box empty, and the frozen engine form beam_analysis takes its default 'simple' silently, with no ask (wL^2/8 = 14.5 where the cantilever's wL^2/2 = 58 is right, 4x too small). The finder-data 'other-beams' not-in-tool signals are literal phrases ('fixed at both ends', 'fixed-fixed beam', 'propped' ...), so 'both ends fixed' and 'fixed at one end and pinned at the other' get through. uniformLoads()/beamAnalysisFields place every klf load on the whole span, and no word for a partial load ('over the left half') is checked. The holdout H11 ('fixed support at the left end and free at the right end') prints the same wrong 14.5 for the same reason. In the corpus, 'fixed' in a beam question appears only as fixity wording.
clusters.fix_plan: [beam-support-and-load-layout] reader.js beamAnalysisFields, right after the cant test (or a helper in a new file called from there; it also runs for beam_select's analysis object, hoist=false). (a) CANTILEVER (ANSWER) when no 'cantilever' word is present but the words say one end is fixed or built in and the other is free: '\bfixed[- ]free\b|\bfree[- ]fixed\b|\b(?:fixed|built[- ]?in(?:to)?|clamped)\b[^.;]{0,50}\bfree\b|\bfree\b[^.;]{0,50}\b(?:fixed|built[- ]?in|wall)\b|\b(?:sticks?|projects?|juts?)\s+out\s+(?:from|of)\s+(?:the\s+|a\s+)?wall', with no pinned|hinged|roller|propped|simply|simple|'both ends'|'at both' in the text. Then support = cantilever: 58 kip-ft for 182/183/184/196 and H11 (the page's own cantilever path already gives 58, A2-beam-163..165). (b) STOP, kind 'stop', one sentence with no number ('NOT answered here: this page works out simple spans and cantilevers only; if the other end is free, type the word cantilever'), for any other fixity word in a beam part: \bfixed\b|\bbuilt[- ]?in(?:to)?\b|\bclamped\b|\bencastr|\bpropped\b|\brestrained\s+against\s+rotation. This covers 'fixed at one end' or 'built into a wall at one end' with the other end not stated (144, 153: two readings, so never choose), fixed-pinned (185, 227) and 'both ends fixed' (186). (c) The same STOP for a uniform load on part of the span: '\bover\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:left|right|middle|central|cent(?:er|re)|first|last|end)\s+(?:half|third|quarter|portion|part|\d)|\bover\s+(?:one\s+|a\s+|the\s+)?(?:half|third|quarter|portion|part)\s+of\b|\bpartial(?:ly)?\s+(?:span|uniform|distributed|loaded|load)|\bfrom\s+x\s*=' (64). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'cantilever' in any spelling the spelling map fixes, including point loads measured 'from the free end/wall'; 'simply supported' / 'simple span'; beams 'supported on (masonry) walls' or a 'bearing wall' (no fixity word); 'fully braced' and 'braced' (not fixity); 'over the entire/full/whole span or length'; the finder's other-beams refusals (A2-beam-39, A2-beam-210). Run regress.sh and read every changed beam line.

clusters.title: A length written in feet and inches (20'-6", 8 ft 6 in) keeps only the feet in span, length and spacing
clusters.root_cause: [ft-in-lengths] reader.js findLengths (1284-1370). Every one-length rule builds its item through mk() from the feet number only: span 1318, 'N-ft span' 1325, 'span is' 1328, length/height 1332, spacing 1345/1348/1350. The ft-in regex at 1294 stores the full value in L.combos, but combos are used only when no span at all was read (beamAnalysisFields 2170). They are never used for spacing (floorBits) or by beam_max_live_load (2315 takes span || length). So 20'-6" becomes 20 ft, and 'spaced 8 ft 6 in' becomes 8 ft. The leftover '6 in' is hidden from the unplaced-number gate whenever another field quotes the same digit ('6 in slab').
clusters.fix_plan: [ft-in-lengths] One post-pass at the end of findLengths (reader.js). For L.span, L.length and L.spacing in ft: if a combo starts inside the item's match and ends after it (the inches follow the feet directly) and its inch part is < 12, replace the item with the combo (value ft + in/12, 'from' running through the inches, rule 'ft-in'). If the inches are directly followed by a thickness or size noun (thick|slab|deck|concrete|plate|bolt|dia|hole|deep|depth|wide|flange|web|leg), as in his comma-less 'spaced 8 ft 6 in slab', there are two readings: do not choose, ASK kind 'need' on that length. I prototyped this on a scratch copy and ran all 4,718 corpus questions: 16 change, every one to the right value (181: 243.75; 67: 209.4; loads-08: 1.445; also A2-beam-215/216/217/43 and loads-p40/58/59/76/78/79/80/81/82/165, where three refusals now answer 1.3175) and nothing regresses. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'L = 18 ft 6 in' (the labelled rule already adds the inches); '3 spaces of 6 ft 8 in'; a span given in inches ('246 in', already right); '6 in slab' as the slab thickness; column lengths given with labels.
